name: a token signed with an algorithm this server does not use
why: The stack the CLI brings up takes an HS512 token signed with the project secret and postgrest 16.1 refuses it, so this case can only match one of the two and it matches the version the suite is recorded from. A secret is a secret whatever the digest over it is, which is why the older build takes it, and refusing an algorithm nobody was asked for is the safer of the two answers. Only known against the live stack: the recording still holds zou to PGRST301 here.

name: a bracket inside a name in an embed
why: zou's rule for a bare name takes bytes upstream's has no room for, so the bracket goes through the parser and into the query, and what refuses is postgres with 42703 rather than the parser with PGRST100. Both answer 400 and neither reads the request. tamnd/zou#167.

name: a json path on the name of an embed
why: Same rule seen from the other side: zou reads projects->name as a json path on a column called projects, and postgres says there is no such column, where upstream refuses the shape in the parser. Both answer 400. tamnd/zou#167.

name: a json path on the name of a spread embed
why: The one of these that goes the other way. Upstream reads ...projects->name(*) and answers 200 with the table's own columns, having quietly dropped the spread, and zou refuses it with PGRST100. Matching the 200 would mean copying a shape upstream ignores rather than serving anything a client asked for, so this is written down rather than followed. tamnd/zou#167.

name: two columns inside an order on an embed
why: Both refuse with PGRST100 and both name the same input. The position and the set of things that would have been taken differ, because zou's order parser gives up where the second column starts and upstream's gives up where the bracket does. tamnd/zou#167.

name: a spread embed under another name
why: Both refuse with PGRST100 at the same character. Upstream's list of what it would have taken names the colon its alias branch could still have taken and zou's does not, so the two messages differ by three words. tamnd/zou#167.
